lesson.subject: english
lesson.title: Writing with Style
lesson.summary: Make writing come alive with similes, metaphors, joining words and well-planned paragraphs.
learning_objectives: Tell a simile from a metaphor and use both
Join ideas with because, although and while
Plan a paragraph with a topic sentence and details
Build a strong description with an expanded noun phrase

blocks.markdown:
Last week you looked at the jobs words do.

This week you will use those words like a real author.

We will paint pictures with language.

blocks.alt: Great writers paint pictures with words.
blocks.caption: Great writers paint pictures with words.

blocks.markdown:
A **simile** compares two things using **like** or **as**. 'She was as quick as a cheetah.'

A **metaphor** says one thing is another thing. 'The moon was a silver coin.'

scenes.caption: Simile: The moon was like a silver coin.
Metaphor: The moon was a silver coin.

options.text: She was as brave as a lion.

question.prompt: 'The classroom was a zoo.' What is this?

blocks.markdown: Writers all over the world use similes. In Urdu poems too, a smile can be 'bright as the moon'.

A **conjunction** joins two ideas. **Because** gives a reason. **Although** shows a surprise. **While** shows two things happening at once.

Fatima took an umbrella **because** it was raining. **Although** it was cold, she went outside. She read **while** the rain fell.

blocks.alt: Because, although and while join ideas.
blocks.caption: Because, although and while join ideas.

question.prompt: Which word fits? ___ the sun was hot, we played outside.
Match the joining word to its job.

blocks.markdown:
An **expanded noun phrase** adds describing words to a noun. 'The tree' becomes 'the tall, old tree by the river'.

Each describing word helps the reader see a clearer picture.

scenes.caption: The tall, old tree by the river.

question.prompt: Which is an expanded noun phrase?

options.text: the tall, old tree by the river

blocks.title: Describe a picture
instructions: Look out of the window or at a photo.
Write one simple sentence about what you see.
Make it better with an expanded noun phrase, a simile and a joining word.

blocks.markdown:
A **paragraph** is a group of sentences about one idea. It starts with a **topic sentence** that tells the reader the main idea. The next sentences add details.

When you change to a new idea, start a new paragraph on a new line.

scenes.caption: The topic sentence says the main idea.
Detail sentences add facts or description.
A new idea starts a new paragraph.

question.prompt: You should start a new paragraph when you move to a new idea.
question.hint: Each paragraph has one main idea.

blocks.prompt: Why is it easier to read a text that has paragraphs?
blocks.answer_markdown: Paragraphs break the text into chunks, so the reader can follow one idea at a time.

points: A simile compares with like or as. A metaphor says something is something else.
Conjunctions join ideas: because, although and while.
An expanded noun phrase paints a clear picture.
A paragraph has one idea and starts with a topic sentence.

blocks.markdown: When you are ready, start the quiz. It has 15 questions and takes about 15 minutes.

terms.meaning: A comparison that uses like or as, such as 'as quick as a cheetah'.
A word used in a simile to compare two things.
A word used in a simile, like in 'as brave as a lion'.
A comparison that says one thing is another thing, such as 'the moon was a coin'.
A word that joins two ideas.
A conjunction that gives a reason.
A conjunction that shows a surprise or a difference.
A conjunction that shows two things happening at the same time.
A noun with extra describing words, like 'the tall, old tree by the river'.
A group of sentences about one idea.
The sentence that tells the reader the main idea of a paragraph.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a simile?
questions.explanation: A simile compares using like or as.

questions.prompt: 'The sun is a golden coin.' What is this?
questions.hint: It says the sun IS a coin.
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing is another.

questions.prompt: Which of these are similes? Pick all that apply.
questions.explanation: Similes use as or like. The others are metaphors.

options.text: The sun is a golden coin

questions.prompt: 'The moon was a silver coin.' Tap the thing being described.
questions.hint: Which thing is being compared to a coin?
questions.explanation: The moon is described as a silver coin.

questions.prompt: Match each joining word to its job.
questions.explanation: Because gives a reason, although shows a surprise and while shows two things at once.

questions.prompt: I wore my coat ___ it was cold.
questions.explanation: Because gives the reason for wearing a coat.

questions.prompt: ___ it was raining, we still had a picnic.
questions.explanation: Although shows a surprise: rain, but still a picnic.

questions.prompt: Which group of words is an expanded noun phrase?
questions.explanation: It adds describing words and a place to the noun.

options.text: the shimmering lake beside the mountain

questions.prompt: What do we call a group of sentences about one idea?
questions.explanation: A group of sentences about one idea is a paragraph.

questions.prompt: A topic sentence tells the reader the main idea of the paragraph.
questions.explanation: A topic sentence gives the main idea.

questions.prompt: Put the sentences in order to make a paragraph.
questions.explanation: The topic sentence comes first and the ending sentence comes last.

items.text: It is a day full of joy.
We eat sweet food with family.

questions.prompt: A story has 3 separate ideas. How many paragraphs would you use?
questions.explanation: Each idea gets its own paragraph, so 3.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adjective? The shimmering lake was calm.

questions.explanation: It adds colour, size and light to make a clear picture.

options.text: The huge, golden dome of the mosque glowed in the evening light.
